items.prompt: Which part of a plant grows under the soil?

options.why: The flower grows at the top of the plant, in the light.
Leaves grow above the soil to catch the light.

hints: Think about a plant pulled out of a pot.
Which part is hidden in the soil?
Picture digging up a plant. What do you see at the bottom?
items.explanation: The roots grow under the soil. They hold the plant in place and take in water.

items.prompt: Match each part of the plant to its job.

figure.alt: A flowering plant with roots, a stem, leaves and a flower.

pairs: take in water from the soil
hints: Think about where each part is on the plant.
Start with the part you know best.
The roots are under the soil. What can they find there?
items.explanation: Roots take in water, the stem holds the plant up, leaves make food using light and flowers make seeds.

items.prompt: Which plant part is often green and flat?

options.why: Roots are usually under the soil and look like thin strings.
Seeds are small and often hard and round.

hints: Think about what you see on a tree branch.
Which part catches the light?
Look at a plant near you. Which part is flat?
items.explanation: Most leaves are green and flat. Their flat shape helps them catch light to make food.

items.prompt: Order the parts of a sunflower from the bottom to the top.

figure.alt: A tall sunflower growing in soil.

hints: Start at the soil and move up.
Which part is under the ground?
Put the roots first, then think about what grows out of the soil.
items.explanation: The roots are under the soil. The stem grows up from them, the leaves grow on the stem and the big flower is at the top.

items.prompt: A tree has a thick, woody stem. It is called a ___.

figure.alt: A tree with branches, leaves and a thick woody stem.

hints: Think about the big brown part of a tree.
It holds up all the branches.
Picture hugging a tree. What are your arms around?
items.explanation: The thick, woody stem of a tree is called the trunk. It holds the tree up and carries water to the branches.

items.prompt: Where does this food grow? Sort the cards.

figure.alt: A carrot, an apple and a banana.

hints: Think about where you would dig to find it.
Roots grow under the soil. Fruits grow on the plant above it.
Start with the carrot. Is the orange part a root?
items.explanation: Carrots, cassava and sweet potatoes are roots, so they grow under the soil. Apples, bananas and tomatoes are fruits that grow above the soil.

items.prompt: Which part of a mango tree holds the seed?

options.why: Roots stay under the soil and take in water.
Leaves make food. They do not hold seeds.

hints: Think about what you find inside a mango.
When you eat a mango, what is in the middle?
Picture cutting a mango open.
items.explanation: The mango fruit holds a big seed inside. Fruits grow from flowers and keep the seeds safe.

items.prompt: Which part carries water from the roots to the leaves?

options.why: The flower makes seeds. It is at the top of the stem.
A seed grows into a new plant. It does not carry water.

hints: Water goes up from the bottom of the plant.
Which part joins the roots to the leaves?
Trace a path with your finger from the roots up to a leaf.
items.explanation: The stem carries water from the roots up to the leaves and flowers. It also holds the plant up.

items.prompt: Choose all the parts that grow above the soil on most plants.

options.why: Roots grow down into the soil.

hints: Think about what you can see when you look at a plant in a pot.
Picture the top of the soil. Is each part above it or below it?
Start with the roots. Where do they grow?
items.explanation: Leaves, flowers and the stem grow above the soil. The roots grow down into the soil.

items.prompt: Draw a plant in the soil. Label the roots, stem, leaves and flower.

criteria.label: Draws roots under the soil line
Labels at least three parts correctly

hints: Draw a line for the top of the soil first.
Roots go below the line. The rest of the plant grows above it.
items.explanation: A plant has roots under the soil, a stem that holds it up, leaves that make food and a flower that makes seeds.

items.prompt: Ayu pulls a weed out of the garden. Long thin parts hang from the bottom. What are they?

options.why: Petals are the coloured parts of a flower.
The stem grows above the soil and holds the plant up.

hints: Think about which part was under the soil.
Which part holds a plant in the ground?
Picture the weed before Ayu pulled it. What was hidden?
items.explanation: The long thin parts are roots. They grew under the soil, held the weed in place and took in water.

items.prompt: A cactus has sharp spines instead of flat leaves. Which part stores water?

figure.alt: A cactus with a thick green stem covered in sharp spines.

options.why: Spines are thin and sharp. They keep animals away.
The flower makes seeds. It is too small to store much water.

hints: Look at which part of the cactus is fat and green.
Spines are thin. Could they hold much water?
Find the thickest part of the cactus in the picture.
items.explanation: A cactus stores water in its thick, green stem. This helps it live in dry places like deserts. The spines keep animals away.
